paras.text: Oxidation states of atoms depend upon unpaired electrons in d-orbitals. Compounds of vanadium in +5, +4, +3 and +2 oxidation states are important.
paras.urdu: ایٹموں کی تکسیدی حالتیں d آربیٹل کے غیر جوڑی دار الیکٹرانوں پر منحصر ہیں۔ وینیڈیم کی +5، +4، +3 اور +2 حالتوں کے مرکبات اہم ہیں۔

paras.text: The compounds in the lower oxidation state are good reducing agents. They also have ionic character and due to incomplete electron sub-shell they are also coloured. The compounds in the higher oxidation states are generally colourless due to the empty electron shell. When a colourless compound of V⁵⁺(3d⁰, 4s⁰) is reduced by suitable reducing agent, it first turns blue VO²⁺ (3d¹, 4s⁰), then green V³⁺(3d², 4s⁰) and finally violet V²⁺(3d³, 4s⁰). Vanadium also shows +1, 0, −1 oxidation states in the compounds [V(dipy)₃]¹⁺, V(CO)₆ and [V(CO)₆]¹⁻ respectively.
paras.urdu: کم تکسیدی حالت کے مرکبات اچھے تخفیفی عامل ہیں۔ وہ آئنک بھی ہیں اور نامکمل الیکٹرانی ذیلی خول کی وجہ سے رنگین بھی ہیں۔ زیادہ تکسیدی حالت کے مرکبات خالی الیکٹرانی خول کی وجہ سے عموماً بے رنگ ہیں۔ V⁵⁺(3d⁰, 4s⁰) کا بے رنگ مرکب مناسب تخفیفی عامل سے تخفیف پائے تو پہلے نیلا VO²⁺(3d¹, 4s⁰)، پھر سبز V³⁺(3d², 4s⁰) اور آخر بنفشی V²⁺(3d³, 4s⁰) بنتا ہے۔ وینیڈیم بالترتیب [V(dipy)₃]¹⁺، V(CO)₆ اور [V(CO)₆]¹⁻ میں +1، 0 اور −1 حالتیں بھی دکھاتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د ټیټ اکسیدېشن حالت مرکبات ښه احیاکوونکي دي. ایوني طبیعت هم لري او د نیمګړي الکتروني فرعي پوښ له امله رنګین هم دي. د لوړ اکسیدېشن حالت مرکبات د تش الکتروني پوښ له امله عموماً بې رنګه دي. که د V⁵⁺(3d⁰, 4s⁰) بې رنګه مرکب په مناسب احیاکوونکي احیا شي، لومړی نیلي VO²⁺(3d¹, 4s⁰)، بیا شین V³⁺(3d², 4s⁰) او په پای کې بنفشي V²⁺(3d³, 4s⁰) جوړېږي. وناډیم په ترتیب سره په [V(dipy)₃]¹⁺، V(CO)₆ او [V(CO)₆]¹⁻ کې +1، 0 او −1 حالتونه هم ښيي.

paras.text: Chromium, symbol Cr, atomic number 24 and atomic mass is 51.99 a.m.u, is a shiny metallic element. Chromium metal provides a shiny protective coating for iron and steel surfaces due to brilliant and corrosion resistant nature. Chromium metal is not inert in itself; instead, it forms a very thin, tough and transparent oxide coating that gives protection.

paras.pashto: کرومیم، نښه Cr، اټومي شمېره 24 او اټومي کتله 51.99 a.m.u.، ځلېدونکی فلزي عنصر دی. د ځلا او زنګ پر وړاندې د مقاومت له امله د اوسپنې او فولادو پر سطحو ځلېدونکی محافظتي پوښ جوړوي. کرومیم په خپله غیر فعال نه دی؛ بلکې ډېر نری، کلک او شفاف اکسایډ پوښ جوړوي چې ساتنه برابروي.

sections.theory:
14.3 Chemistry of Some important Transition Elements

14.3.1 Vanadium

Vanadium symbol ‘V’, silvery white metallic element with an atomic number of 23 and atomic mass 50.941 a.m.u. Vanadium is used for vanadium steels, a particularly hard alloy employed for knife blades and various workshop tools.

14.3.1.1 Oxidation States

Oxidation states of atoms depend upon unpaired electrons in d-orbitals. Compounds of vanadium in +5, +4, +3 and +2 oxidation states are important.

The compounds in the lower oxidation state are good reducing agents. They also have ionic character and due to incomplete electron sub-shell they are also coloured. The compounds in the higher oxidation states are generally colourless due to the empty electron shell. When a colourless compound of V⁵⁺(3d⁰, 4s⁰) is reduced by suitable reducing agent, it first turns blue VO²⁺ (3d¹, 4s⁰), then green V³⁺(3d², 4s⁰) and finally violet V²⁺(3d³, 4s⁰). Vanadium also shows +1, 0, −1 oxidation states in the compounds [V(dipy)₃]¹⁺, V(CO)₆ and [V(CO)₆]¹⁻ respectively.

Tidbit — Difference between Valency and Oxidation Number

Valency is different from the oxidation number. Thus, the valency of nitrogen is 3, whereas it can have oxidation numbers from −3 to +5. The oxidation number is the hypothetical charge of an atom in a molecule or ion, and it is a measure of its apparent capacity to gain or lose electrons within that species.

14.3.1.2 As Catalyst in Contact Process

The contact process is the common method of producing sulphuric acid in high concentrations needed for industrial process.

Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) is used as a catalyst in various oxidation reactions involving the use of oxygen (O₂) as the oxidizing agent e.g. conversion of SO₂ to SO₃ in the manufacture of H₂SO₄.

2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) — V₂O₅ (400–450°C)

14.3.2 Chromium

Chromium, symbol Cr, atomic number 24 and atomic mass is 51.99 a.m.u, is a shiny metallic element. Chromium metal provides a shiny protective coating for iron and steel surfaces due to brilliant and corrosion resistant nature. Chromium metal is not inert in itself; instead, it forms a very thin, tough and transparent oxide coating that gives protection.

14.3.2.1 Oxidation States

Chromium forms three common oxidation states in its compounds, +2, +3 and +6. Chromium in +3 oxidation state is most stable, while Cr(+2) compounds are not much stable and are strong reducing agents, while those of Cr(+6) compounds are strong oxidizing agents.

With the increase in oxidation state of the chromium,

a. The acidic character of its oxides also increases.

b. Similarly the covalent character of the compounds also increases. Thus, Cr(+2) compounds are ionic, Cr(+3) compounds ionize to some extent, while those of Cr(+6) are covalent.

The compounds in which chromium shows +2 oxidation state are called chromous salts. These salts are unstable and tend to oxidize on exposure to air into corresponding Cr(+3) compounds. Some of chromous salts are CrCl₂, CrS, CrSO₄.7H₂O, CrCO₃ etc.

The compounds in which chromium shows +3 oxidation state are called chromic compounds. These may be derived from chromic oxide, Cr₂O₃. These are formed as chromate or dichromate. Examples of chromic compounds are chromic chloride (CrCl₃), chromic sulphate, Cr₂(SO₄)₃.18H₂O.

b. همدارنګه د مرکباتو اشتراکي طبیعت هم زیاتېږي. د Cr(+2) مرکبات ایوني دي، د Cr(+3) مرکبات تر یوه حده ایونونه جوړوي، خو د Cr(+6) مرکبات اشتراکي دي.

14.3 Chemistry of Some important Transition Elements

14.3.1 Vanadium

Vanadium symbol ‘V’, silvery white metallic element with an atomic number of 23 and atomic mass 50.941 a.m.u. Vanadium is used for vanadium steels, a particularly hard alloy employed for knife blades and various workshop tools.

14.3.1.1 Oxidation States

Oxidation states of atoms depend upon unpaired electrons in d-orbitals. Compounds of vanadium in +5, +4, +3 and +2 oxidation states are important.

The compounds in the lower oxidation state are good reducing agents. They also have ionic character and due to incomplete electron sub-shell they are also coloured. The compounds in the higher oxidation states are generally colourless due to the empty electron shell. When a colourless compound of V⁵⁺(3d⁰, 4s⁰) is reduced by suitable reducing agent, it first turns blue VO²⁺ (3d¹, 4s⁰), then green V³⁺(3d², 4s⁰) and finally violet V²⁺(3d³, 4s⁰). Vanadium also shows +1, 0, −1 oxidation states in the compounds [V(dipy)₃]¹⁺, V(CO)₆ and [V(CO)₆]¹⁻ respectively.

Tidbit — Difference between Valency and Oxidation Number

Valency is different from the oxidation number. Thus, the valency of nitrogen is 3, whereas it can have oxidation numbers from −3 to +5. The oxidation number is the hypothetical charge of an atom in a molecule or ion, and it is a measure of its apparent capacity to gain or lose electrons within that species.

14.3.1.2 As Catalyst in Contact Process

The contact process is the common method of producing sulphuric acid in high concentrations needed for industrial process.

Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) is used as a catalyst in various oxidation reactions involving the use of oxygen (O₂) as the oxidizing agent e.g. conversion of SO₂ to SO₃ in the manufacture of H₂SO₄.

2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) — V₂O₅ (400–450°C)

14.3.2 Chromium

Chromium, symbol Cr, atomic number 24 and atomic mass is 51.99 a.m.u, is a shiny metallic element. Chromium metal provides a shiny protective coating for iron and steel surfaces due to brilliant and corrosion resistant nature. Chromium metal is not inert in itself; instead, it forms a very thin, tough and transparent oxide coating that gives protection.

14.3.2.1 Oxidation States

Chromium forms three common oxidation states in its compounds, +2, +3 and +6. Chromium in +3 oxidation state is most stable, while Cr(+2) compounds are not much stable and are strong reducing agents, while those of Cr(+6) compounds are strong oxidizing agents.

With the increase in oxidation state of the chromium,

a. The acidic character of its oxides also increases.

b. Similarly the covalent character of the compounds also increases. Thus, Cr(+2) compounds are ionic, Cr(+3) compounds ionize to some extent, while those of Cr(+6) are covalent.

The compounds in which chromium shows +2 oxidation state are called chromous salts. These salts are unstable and tend to oxidize on exposure to air into corresponding Cr(+3) compounds. Some of chromous salts are CrCl₂, CrS, CrSO₄.7H₂O, CrCO₃ etc.

The compounds in which chromium shows +3 oxidation state are called chromic compounds. These may be derived from chromic oxide, Cr₂O₃. These are formed as chromate or dichromate. Examples of chromic compounds are chromic chloride (CrCl₃), chromic sulphate, Cr₂(SO₄)₃.18H₂O.
